standard_prerequisites.name: The monoidal structure on graded vector spaces
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the tensor product, the associativity constraints and the unit of the monoidal category in which the left dual is taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dual objects in a monoidal category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the evaluation and coevaluation maps together with the two identities that the proof unfolds.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 4290-4296): with the unit taken to be the field placed in degree 0, the evaluation becomes a family of pairings W^{-n} x V^n -> F, and the author chooses bases of the graded pieces of V.

Finiteness (proof lines 4297-4307): writing the coevaluation of 1 as a finite sum of elementary tensors, the identity that the composite of evaluation and coevaluation is the identity on W shows that W is generated as a graded vector space by the finitely many nonzero vectors occurring in that sum; consequently the sum of the dimensions of the graded pieces of V is finite.

Nondegeneracy (proof lines 4308-4323): the other identity, that the composite in the opposite order is the identity on V, evaluated at a basis vector gives the orthogonality relation among the vectors extracted from the coevaluation, from which the author concludes that they form the dual basis of each graded piece of W, so the pairings are nondegenerate.
proof_roadmap: Read the evaluation as a family of pairings using that the unit sits in degree 0.
Use the triangle identity for the coevaluation to show that W is generated by finitely many vectors coming from a finite sum.
Use the other triangle identity to identify the dual bases and get nondegeneracy.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a graded vector space admitting a left dual in the monoidal category of graded vector spaces has finite total dimension and that the evaluation gives nondegenerate pairings between opposite graded pieces (statement lines 4280-4288). The proof is a complete argument: the unit is identified with the field in degree 0 so that the evaluation becomes a family of pairings (proof lines 4290-4296); the first triangle identity expresses the identity on W through a finite sum and hence shows that W is generated by finitely many vectors, which gives finiteness of the total dimension of V (proof lines 4297-4307); the second triangle identity evaluated on basis vectors produces the dual-basis relation and hence nondegeneracy (proof lines 4308-4323). The non-formal content is the extraction of the dual basis from the two identities. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
